name: Large Electron-Positron Collider
notes: Per-beam energies (≈45.5 GeV at LEP1, ≈104.5 GeV at LEP2) are recorded as derived halves of the sourced centre-of-mass energies; home.cern quotes only the collision energies.

circumference.quote: With its 27-kilometre circumference, the Large Electron-Positron (LEP) collider was - and still is - the largest electron-positron accelerator ever built.

cms_energy.note: Maximum centre-of-mass energy reached, at the end of LEP2.
cms_energy.quote: The collider's energy eventually topped 209 GeV in 2000.

summary.plain: The largest electron-positron collider ever built: a 27-kilometre ring under the Swiss-French border that ran from 1989 to 2000 and produced about 17 million Z particles. Its tunnel was then reused for the Large Hadron Collider.
summary.technical: 27 km e⁺e⁻ storage-ring collider with four experiments (ALEPH, DELPHI, L3, OPAL). LEP1 ran at the Z pole (~91 GeV cms); after the 1995 upgrade LEP2 reached 209 GeV cms in 2000. Closed 2 November 2000; its tunnel now houses the LHC.
